analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: STABLE START
key_insights: US equities rallied broadly on 10/26: S&P +70bps at 7,676, NDX +109bps at 29,273, R2K +42bps at 2,787, Dow +28bps at 52,361. The desk links the bounce to signs of AI stabilization, with a MOC imbalance of $3.5bn to sell.
The desk sees little sign of offense in AI/Tech. The bounces of the last two weeks, including today's, are mostly from the end of high-velocity supply, not new buying.
Desk activity was muted ahead of a busy week. Central bank decisions include the FOMC, BOC, ECB and BOJ. Roughly 44% of SPX market cap reports earnings, led by MSFT, GOOG, AMZN and INTC.

Brazil/EWZ fell about 20% in one session, its worst outside Covid (-23%). President Lula won the presidential race despite a first-round deficit, against prediction market expectations. Polymarket has now been wrong on only three presidential elections.
Floor activity scored 4 out of 10 and overall flow skews were benign. Volume was 16.630bn shares against a year-to-date daily average of 18.513bn.

Derivatives: skew collapsed coming out of the weekend and spot vol compressed with the rally. NDX vol underperformed significantly despite tech-led gains, which highlights the steep NDX/S&P vol spread.

The desk favors short-dated QQQ call spreads to capture a potential positioning squeeze through the upcoming earnings and election catalysts. The QQQ 13Nov 735/755 call spread pays just under 5x gross.

Single-stock flows were muted with building investor anxiety, reflecting persistent tech de-risking across the street. AMZN stands out ahead of Thursday's earnings, with the stock over 12% off its August highs. The desk prefers capped upside structures out to December.
Tomorrow's S&P implied move was priced at 50bps. The desk expects daily straddles to stay in that range.
